description: Somos un equipo que participa en NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 con el objetivo de desarrollar una solución de software para apoyar el monitoreo de la salud de astronautas durante misiones espaciales de larga duración.
summary: ORVITA is an innovative astronaut health and medical monitoring software developed for deep space missions like Artemis-IV. Long-duration spaceflight exposes crews to radiation, isolation, altered gravity, and closed environments that trigger severe physical and mental health risks. Because communication delays with Earth prevent immediate medical assistance, ORVITA empowers astronauts with complete operational autonomy. The platform combines a clean, human-centered "Deep Space" UI with 8 core modules—including real-time biometric tracking, an interactive 3D Body Explorer for precise symptom logging, step-by-step clinical guidance, and a visual virtual pharmacy inventory tracking medication expiration dates and microgravity antibiotic/insulin fermentation batches. By correlating daily symptoms and clinical data with personal medical histories, ORVITA generates smart alerts and actionable self-care recommendations, protecting crew vitality and ensuring mission success.
details:
What it does exactly?: ORVITA is an innovative astronaut health and medical monitoring software developed for long-duration deep space missions like Artemis-IV. It empowers crew members to independently log, evaluate, and manage their physical health, mental well-being, and medical supplies without relying on Earth control.

How it works?: It operates through a centralized dashboard linked to 8 interactive modules. Astronauts log daily biometrics (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, and mood) or use the interactive 3D Body Explorer by tapping a specific body part experiencing discomfort to instantly retrieve targeted diagnostic guidance. The system cross-references these inputs with personal medical histories to trigger smart clinical alerts and preventative care recommendations.

What benefits does it offer?: It provides a rapid, centralized overview of physical and behavioral health status, early detection of deep-space biological risks (bone density loss, circadian fatigue, psychological isolation), out-of-range alerts, and a visual pharmacy inventory tracking stock levels, expiration dates, and active microgravity antibiotic/insulin fermentation batches.

What do we hope to achieve?: To guarantee crew autonomy and vitality during deep space exploration missions (Moon and Mars), minimizing human error, protecting physical and mental well-being, and establishing a new standard for preventive aerospace and terrestrial medicine.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did we use?: UI prototyping and architecture via Google Stitch.ai and Figma; technical development coordinated in Visual Studio Code; presentation design in Canva (leveraging official ISS media assets and open-source Inter and IBM Plex Mono typography); and AI assistance tools (Gemini and Claude) for research synthesis and prompt engineering.
projectRefs: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
